extracted.intended_audience: general tech and social-media news readers; YouTube creators
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes a YouTube creator's violation of platform rules for filming a suicide victim and explains YouTube's standards and typical consequences; useful for creators or reporters assessing acceptable/forbidden video content. Covers graphic-content rules, contextual exceptions, and expected creator responses (removal/apology).

rubrics_metrics.name: YouTube prohibition on shocking/sensational graphic content
rubrics_metrics.description: “YouTube prohibits violent or gory content posted in a shocking, sensational or disrespectful manner.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit platform standard cited by YouTube. Content that depicts violence or gore in ways that are intended to shock or sensationalize is disallowed. The statement is used by the platform when explaining removals and community enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions under which graphic content may remain
rubrics_metrics.description: “If a video is graphic, it can only remain on the site when supported by appropriate educational or documentary information and in some cases it will be age-gated.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted exceptions require clear educational or documentary context and may trigger age-gating; platforms may also partner with safety organizations (e.g., National Suicide Prevention Lifeline) and surface educational resources (YouTube Safety Center) alongside such content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for victims and families / avoid disrespectful posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Content showing deceased individuals (e.g., apparent suicide victims) should not be posted in disrespectful or exploitative ways; platforms and public opinion expect dignity and sensitivity toward victims and their families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the article, the platform’s statement—“Our hearts go out to the family of the person featured in the video”—illustrates the expectation of respect. Creators should avoid zoomed-in or sensational footage of deceased persons and consider the impact on families and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for violating content and conduct standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Creators who post prohibited or offensive material risk content removal, public backlash, calls for banning, loss of brand deals, and professional consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the article: removal of the video; public criticism and calls to ban the creator from YouTube; Disney cutting ties with creators (PewDiePie) after offensive content; Jake Paul losing a Disney Channel job following problematic behavior. Platform enforcement and corporate responses both drive consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public apology and remedial actions after inappropriate content
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate creator response includes removing the offending content, apologizing publicly, acknowledging harm (to viewers and victims/families), and clarifying intent (e.g., not doing it for views).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article documents Logan Paul removing the video, posting a Twitter apology stating he was “sorry” and hadn’t “done it for views,” and posting a follow-up apology video explicitly apologizing to those affected and the victim’s family. These actions are presented as the visible remediation pattern expected after such incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of hate speech and other offensive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of racial slurs, anti-semitic content, or similarly offensive material is grounds for losing platform support or corporate relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited example: Disney cut ties with PewDiePie after he used a racial slur and had posted anti-semitic content. Creators should avoid hate speech and discriminatory content to prevent account penalties and loss of partnerships.
